articles.title: Real Madrid v Inter, Millwall v Newcastle: Champions League and Carabao Cup – live
articles.summary: Champions League: Lille v Betis, Dortmund v Villarreal. Carabao Cup: Palace v Middlesbrough, Sunderland v Hull. Live scores | Read Football Daily | And email Daniel. Inter, meanwhile, look solid. They’ve won three from three in Serie A, and will, I think, look to clutter the centre of the pitch.
body: Our main focus here, though, will be on Madrid v Inter. Mourinho’s men lost at Betis last weekend, and are without the suspended Eduardo Camvinga, Bernardo Silva and Arda Guler. As such Trent Alexander-Arnold comes in on the right of the central three – a move I doubt Aurelien Tchouameni likes all that much. I can’t say I think Alexander-Arnold is much use in that position – as Gary Neville once noted, most right-backs are failed midfielders – but he’s capable of creating something from nothing. I guess I’d quite like to see Yan Diomande on the right, but i’m not surprised Mourinho wants the extra body in midfield that Brahim Diaz can become.

articles.title: Cullen leads late Pears rally against Northants
articles.summary: Henry Cullen and Jake Libby hit half-centuries as Worcestershire recover from a mid-innings slump in their County Championship game against Northants.
body: Northamptonshire skipper Luke Procter took 5-63 to help his promotion-chasing side bowl out Worcestershire for 200, but not before the hosts were bolstered by a late-order maiden half-century from Henry Cullen.
The young wicketkeeper made 64 following Jake Libby's earlier half-century (55), while Adam Hose (45) was the only other man in double figures.
Supported by Harry Conway (2-38), Procter led from the front as the Pears middle order slumped from 103-2 to 150-9, before Cullen's late counter-offensive.
Northants openers Ricardo Vasconcelos and Procter, who was struck a painful blow amidships, then negotiated a tricky eight-over spell late in the day to close on 16-0.

articles.title: Air traffic chaos delays Arsenal flight to Naples for Champions League
articles.summary: Team arriving late at their hotel in southern Italy. Jurriën Timber in squad for first time since May. Arsenal’s preparations for their opening Champions League game against Napoli have been disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos that affected airports across the United Kingdom.
body: Mikel Arteta was forced to cancel his pre-match press conference at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Tuesday after Arsenal’s flight was severely delayed by an air-traffic control issue. The Arsenal manager and his players are understood to have remained at the club’s training ground in Hertfordshire as they waited for the delay to pass after completing their morning session as usual.

Club sources have insisted there has been no alteration to their planned schedule other than arriving later than expected to the team hotel. Uefa has also agreed to allow Arsenal to cancel their mandatory press conference due to the delays, which have also affected supporters travelling to Italy for the match.

Jurriën Timber is set to be part of the Arsenal squad for the first time since the Champions League final defeat to Paris Saint-Germain on 30 May after recovering from a groin injury. The Netherlands defender missed the World Cup due to the problem that has dogged him since March but Arteta said before Sunday’s win over Chelsea that Timber was close to returning.

articles.title: Iowa marching band member taken off life support after collapse in extreme heat
articles.summary: Derek Phillips suffered cardiac arrest at football game. Temperatures reached 94F in Iowa City on Saturday. University has not said whether heat caused collapse. A University of Iowa marching band member has been taken off life support after collapsing during extreme heat at the Hawkeyes’…
body: Derek Phillips, a third-year student from Dubuque, Iowa, suffered a sudden cardiac arrest shortly before the band was scheduled to perform its half-time show against Northern Illinois at Kinnick Stadium, according to a message posted to his Instagram account by his family.

Phillips was taken to University of Iowa Health Care, where he was treated in intensive care. His family said the cardiac arrest caused severe brain damage and that they made the decision to remove him from life support.

“Derek is comfortable, surrounded by family, and enveloped in the music he loved so much,” the family said. “Thank you for every prayer, every shared experience, and every bit of love you’ve given to our boy.”
Temperatures reached 94F (34C) in Iowa City on Saturday. It was 90F (32C) at kickoff, making it the fourth-hottest home football game in Iowa history, according to the university.

articles.title: Morgan stars as Middlesex bowl out battling Durham
articles.summary: Ben Raine leads a Durham fightback with the bat after Seb Morgan's four wickets had put Middlesex in the driving seat on day one at Chester-le-Street.
body: Ben Raine led a Durham fightback with the bat after Seb Morgan's four wickets had put Middlesex in the driving seat on the opening day of their County Championship fixture.
An even morning session burst into life in the final over, with Morgan taking two wickets from three balls to put promotion-chasing Durham in a spot of bother at 80-4.

Morgan got the key wicket of Durham skipper Alex Lees just after lunch and a rain delay halted Middlesex's progress for a brief period. Ryan Higgins then picked up the baton upon resumption with three wickets.
However, Durham fought back through a final wicket stand of 90 between Raine (58*) and Callum Parkinson (26) before they were bowled out for 252.

articles.title: Andersson leads Derbyshire fightback against Kent
articles.summary: Martin Andersson held up Kent's promotion advance by leading Derbyshire's fightback on the opening day of the County Championship match at the OurCoop County Ground.
body: The all-rounder scored his third century of the season to guide his team to respectability after Bangladesh pace bowler Hasan Mahmud took two wickets with the first two balls of the game.

Mahmud bowled superbly to claim 4-30 but Andersson was equally impressive with an unbeaten 129 from 190 balls, sharing stands of 91 with Luis Reece (32) and 84 for the eighth wicket with Brett Randell (29).
Derbyshire's cause was also helped by 47 extras as they recovered to post 300 before Ben Aitchison removed Ben Compton to leave Kent on 11-1 at the close.
Kent rested leading wicket-taker Matt Milnes but Mahmud had Derbyshire reeling after the first two balls of an overcast morning.

articles.title: When will Africa get its next Ballon d'Or winner?
articles.summary: Sadio Mane and Achraf Hakimi have been nominated for this year's Ballon d'Or - but when will an African claim football's top individual prize for the first time since 1995?
body: Africa has only ever had one Ballon d'Or winner, and the wait for someone to emulate George Weah is likely to be extended further after this year's nominations were revealed.
Morocco captain Achraf Hakimi and Senegal forward Sadio Mane are the continent's two names on the 30-strong list.

Both players have previously recorded top-six Ballon d'Or finishes but, after a year in which Spain lifted the Fifa World Cup and Kylian Mbappe netted 10 goals to become the tournament's all-time top scorer, the chances of the Paris St-Germain right-back or the Al-Nassr winger lifting the coveted trophy appear slim.
And it is not the first time that Africa has failed to make a big impact.

articles.title: Feyenoord defender Mika Marmol: ‘Barcelona are always favourites to win the Champions League’
articles.summary: As FC Barcelona take on Feyenoord tomorrow in the UEFA Champions League, they will come up against two familiar faces. Indeed, the Dutch giants are managed by ex-Barça defender Giovanni van Bronckhorst, while former La Masia defender Mika Marmol is a part of their squad.
body: Since leaving Barcelona in 2022, the defender had spells with Andorra and Las Palmas, before the 25-year-old joined Feyenoord this summer.
Marmol made one first-team appearance for the Catalan club. And he will make his Champions League debut on Wednesday in a special setting, back at the Spotify Camp Nou.

“I’m very happy to be back here. I think making your debut in this competition is special in itself, and even more so when it happens at the club where I was developed,” Marmol said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo.
The 25-year-old defender, who can play at centre-back and left-back, could be tasked with defending against fellow La Masia graduate Lamine Yamal.

articles.title: Vote for the Hillsdale County ISD Week 2 football player of the week
articles.summary: A career night for Milks, another big game for Towne and six touchdowns from Peiffer were some of Hillsdale County's top performances from Week 2.
body: HILLSDALE COUNTY — Week 2 of the high school football season featured breakthrough wins, rivalry games and one of the biggest individual performances in Hillsdale County history.
Before getting to this week’s standouts, three seniors earned the first Player of the Week honors of the 2026 season.

Jonesville running back John Milks was named the Hillsdale Daily News Player of the Week after rushing for 265 yards and three touchdowns in the Comets’ 34-28 win over Hillsdale. Camden-Frontier quarterback Hunter Sigler won the 8-player Readers’ Choice award after throwing for 126 yards and four touchdowns against Holgate, while Reading quarterback Carter Bassage earned the 11-player Readers’ Choice honor after completing all eight of his passes for 145 yards and two touchdowns in a 48-0 win over East Jackson.

Week 2 brought another deep group of performances, led by Milks putting together a night that will have a place in the Michigan record books. The following list is based on statistics reported to the Daily News before Labor Day on Monday. Some individual statistics were unavailable at publication time.

articles.title: Aston Villa attack clicks in thrilling win over Club Brugge
articles.summary: Aston Villa produced a superb attacking display to end their scoring concerns and begin their Champions League campaign with a thrilling 3-2 win over Club Brugge.
body: The Europa League winners had failed to score in their first three Premier League matches, having had just one shot on target, but their attack clicked in Belgium as John McGinn, Emiliano Buendia and Nicolas Jackson struck to kickstart their season.

Villa had 14 efforts in a scintillating first-half performance that began with McGinn expertly side-footing a trademark first-time shot into the bottom left corner after being set up by Pau Torres' driving run out of defence.

Club Brugge's expansive approach contributed to a breathless tie and the hosts equalised when Hugo Vetlesen swept a low shot into the corner, although Buendia restored Villa's lead within three minutes, tapping in from close range following good work by Joao Gomes.

Villa threatened constantly on the counter-attack and their third goal came when Jackson ran in behind to try and latch onto Torres' long ball forward, beating goalkeeper Yann Sommer to the ball and slotting into an empty net for his first goal since joining in a club-record £65m move.

articles.summary: This article originally appeared on SteelersNOW.com. The Pittsburgh Steelers released their first official depth chart of the season, and Dylan Cook is slotted as the team’s starting right tackle.
body: Head coach Mike McCarthy stopped short of naming Cook as the starter during his Monday press conference. But he hinted that the veteran won the job over rookie Max Iheanachor.
Iheanachor missed the team’s first two preseason games with an undisclosed injury — which appeared to be a neck or shoulder ailment. The time missed set him back in the battle with Cook.
McCarthy said Iheneachor has been impressive but is being cautious due to the time missed.

articles.title: Former NBA standout Robert Covington makes major HBCU hoops move
articles.summary: Former NBA standout Robert Covington makes major HBCU hoops move appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Former NBA standout Robert Covington is making a return to his HBCU in a big way.
body: Covington spoke about his return to Tennessee State in the statement released by the institution.

“I bleed TSU, and I always have,” Covington said. “This is another milestone I’m incredibly grateful for. I’m beyond blessed to now be part of this program full time, and I’m truly excited about what we are building together. This is bigger than basketball. This is about TSU, our people and our program, and building something special that lasts. The best is yet to come.”

“Rob Covington is a major pillar in TSU basketball history and HBCU basketball history,” Smith said. “It is an absolute honor to bring him back to this program. He will wear many hats and will be an important part of where we are going. Rob has become family during my first year in Nashville, and I am beyond excited to continue building with someone who gave his blood, sweat and tears to TSU basketball.”

Covington is the latest former NBA player to lend their talent and experience to HBCU basketball programs. He joins John Wall, Kendrick Perkins, and Monta Ellis, who will each play significant roles in Black college basketball as the new season approaches this Fall.

articles.title: Sabalenka survives Noskova battle to keep US Open three-peat bid alive
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka maintained her hopes of a third successive US Open title with a three-set victory over Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in an absorbing quarter-final - a result that retains her status as world No 1 for at least one more day.
body: The 28-year-old beat Noskova 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7), coming through two tie-breaks - and a 4-2 deficit in the final set - as she sealed victory with a second-serve ace to set up a meeting with the winner of Tuesday night's all-American clash between Jessica Pegula and Emma Navarro in the semi-finals.

Sabalenka needs to win in New York to have any hope of staying as world No 1 but will definitely lose that spot if Elena Rybakina - who defeated Sabalenka in this year's Australian Open final - overcomes Qinwen Zheng in her quarter-final on Wednesday.
If Rybakina is beaten, then Pegula or Coco Gauff could rise to the top of the rankings should they win the tournament at Flushing Meadows on Saturday evening.
Sabalenka, world No 1 for 99 consecutive weeks, is hoping to become the first woman to win the US Open three times in a row since Serena Williams from 2012-14.

articles.title: 'Most pressure in the NFL' Finally Allen's time to win Super Bowl?
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills head coach Joe Brady is under the most pressure in the NFL as he seeks to lead Josh Allen's side from 'bridesmaid to bride', says Sky Sports' Phoebe Schecter.
body: The Bills renew their Super Bowl quest this season having endured more playoff agony earlier this year when they were beaten by the Denver Broncos in overtime of January's Divisional Round clash.

It had been deemed a premature end to one of their best opportunities yet to end prolonged Super Bowl agony, with Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs absent from the playoffs for the first time since 2014 and the likes of Lamar Jackson and Joe Burrow also nowhere to be seen.
Sean McDermott was subsequently fired after nine campaigns in charge, with Brady being promoted to head coach from his post as offensive coordinator.
"Josh Allen will have had a say with Joe Brady coming in and taking on that role," said former Bills coach Schecter on Inside the Huddle.
